pr.title: Don't drop types with no drop glue when building drops for tailcalls
pr.author: WaffleLapkin

issues.title: compiler/rustc_borrowck/src/borrow_set.rs:250:17: found two uses for 2-phase borrow temporary

processing.reason: The PR's wrong transformation only emits a cleanup drop for tail-call argument locals whose type has no drop glue (e.g. `&mut ()``). In Rust's abstract machine, dropping such a value is a runtime no-op: it neither runs a destructor nor invalidates the pointee or the moved value. The historical failure is purely a compile-time borrowck/ICE symptom ("found two uses for 2-phase borrow temporary"), plus MIR storage-marker/backtrace changes. There is no source-grounded, defined runtime execution in which the pre-fix unconditional drop versus the needs_drop-gated drop produces different numeric/boolean/character values while both executions pass Miri. Modeling the erroneous drop as an observable mutation or a borrow-use counter would invent semantics not present in the source program, and making it a real destructor would violate the PR's no-drop-glue precondition. Therefore no valid test_program_pair counterexample exists for this fix.

analysis.originalLogic: In `compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/builder/scope.rs`, when lowering an explicit tail call (`become f(args)`), the builder collected drop obligations for tail-call argument locals. For a local place argument it constructed `Some(DropData { source_info, local, kind: DropKind::Value })` unconditionally, and later iterated `unwind_drops` to emit cleanup drops for every collected `DropData`. The pre-fix test dumps show `_4 = &mut (*_1);` followed by `drop(_3) -> [return: bb2, unwind: bb3];` and a cleanup block dropping `_4`, while `_4` was also moved into the tailcall in `bb2`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to build and emit cleanup/drop glue for every tail-call argument local, including locals whose type has no drop glue (notably `&mut T`). This produced a `drop(_4)` on the unwind path for a `&mut` argument that was simultaneously moved into the tail call. Borrowck then treated that generated drop as a second use of the same two-phase borrow temporary, panicking with `found two uses for 2-phase borrow temporary _4: bb2[1] and bb3[0]`. The fix inserts a `needs_drop` check when creating `DropData` and another `needs_drop` check when iterating `unwind_drops`, so no drop is created for no-drop-glue argument locals.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions using the unstable `explicit_tail_calls` feature (`become f(args)`) where a tail-call argument is a local place whose type has no drop glue, such as a `&mut T` reborrow (`become f(x)` with `x: &mut ()`), especially when the function also has a local that does need dropping (e.g. `let _y = String::new();`) so that a cleanup/unwind path is generated. The triggering domain is argument types for which `ty.needs_drop(...)` is false, not types with real destructors.
analysis.summary: Bug fix for explicit tail calls: while lowering `become` tail-call argument drops, the pre-fix code created drops for locals that do not need dropping, so a moved `&mut` argument also got a cleanup `drop`. Borrowck counted that as a second use of a two-phase borrow temporary and ICE'd. The fix gates both `DropData` construction and later drop emission on `ty.needs_drop(...)`.
analysis.trigger: An explicit tail call `become f(x)` (or recursive `become self.cut()`) where an argument local has a no-drop-glue type such as `&mut T`, combined with a droppable local that creates an unwind path. The generated cleanup drop of the `&mut` argument collides with the argument move as a two-phase borrow use.
preconditions: The crate uses `#![feature(explicit_tail_calls)]` and lowers a `become` tail call through the MIR builder.
At least one tail-call argument is a local place whose type does not need drop (e.g. `&mut T`).
The surrounding scope has a value requiring drop so that an unwind/cleanup block is built for the tail-call argument drops.
Borrow check runs on the resulting MIR and builds a `BorrowSet` that detects two uses of the same two-phase temporary.
pitfalls: Checking only during `DropData` construction is insufficient; the later `unwind_drops` iteration can still emit drops, so both sites must apply the `needs_drop` check.
`StorageDead` removal in MIR tests is an observable consequence of not creating the drop, not an independently targeted change; do not infer that the fix is about storage markers.
Do not generalize the fix to all types: it is specifically about types with no drop glue; droppable tail-call arguments must still receive correct cleanup drops.
The borrowck error is a downstream symptom of malformed MIR; the root cause is in drop elaboration/lowering for tail calls, not in borrow_set itself.
Unwind-path drop generation for a moved argument is distinct from ordinary post-move liveness; the collision is with two-phase borrow temporary bookkeeping.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `tests/ui/explicit-tail-calls/two-phase.rs` `//@ check-pass` regression test using `#![expect(incomplete_features)]` + `#![feature(explicit_tail_calls)]` with a function taking `x: &mut ()`, a droppable local (`let _y = String::new();`), and `become f(x);` to ensure no ICE. Strengthen MIR tests (`tests/mir-opt/tail_call_drops.f.*`, `f_with_arg.*`) to assert that no `drop`/`StorageDead` is emitted for no-drop-glue tail-call argument locals on both `panic-abort` and `panic-unwind` paths, and remove the old `tests/crashes/128097.rs` known-bug entry. Compare the two implementations only by whether a cleanup drop is generated for the non-droppable argument.
evidence: Don't drop types with no drop glue when building drops for tailcalls
The underlying issue is that the current code generates drops for `&mut` which are later counted as a second use of a two-phase temporary:
found two uses for 2-phase borrow temporary _4: bb2[1] and bb3[0]
// this test used to ICE because we tried to run drop glue of `x`
